pr.title: Settle a review thread through project review settle
pr.head: 7d53de38a62498315dbc62b8b28cfb6d5d385a11

summary: A Projector review checks every earlier finding again at each new head. For each finding thread it then settles the thread: it posts a reply that says what it found, and resolves the thread, reopens it, or leaves it open. Until now the reviewer did this by hand. It typed a marker comment, <!-- projector-verify v=1 result=… sha=… model=… -->, at the top of the reply, and ran the resolveReviewThread or unresolveReviewThread GraphQL mutation itself.

The marker matters because the review loop's watcher reads it. When the newest comment on an open finding thread lacks a Projector marker, the watcher treats it as the author answering and asks for a re-review (RESPONDED). A mistyped marker therefore made the reviewer's own reply look like an author's answer. Claude Code's auto mode can also refuse the raw mutations as writes to an external system.

This pull request adds project review settle, which does each step: it writes the marker from the review's saved state, posts the reply as the reviewer, sets the thread's resolution, and reads both back. The review-pr skill now uses it, and project init adds an allow rule for it.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Finding thread: a review thread whose first comment carries the projector-finding marker, which only a Projector review writes.
  • Review state: the file project review setup writes on this machine, recording the head under review, the model, and the reviewer.
  • Reviewer token: a GitHub token for the reviewer account, set for one gh call so the session's own login is left alone.
  • Stack: this pull request sits on #313, which adds project review finish, and this diff is shown against that branch.

groups.title: The settle command
groups.kicker: The new review subcommand and its tests
intro: settle lives in src/projector/review.py, next to census, which lists the finding threads whose ids settle takes. It works in this order:

1. It checks its inputs. It reads the review state and the reply file, and refuses an empty reply or one that already carries a Projector marker.
  2. It checks the thread. finding_thread asks GitHub for the thread and refuses it unless it is a review thread on this pull request whose first comment carries the finding marker.
  3. It posts the reply first. The reply opens with the marker, filled from the state's head SHA and model. When the thread's last comment already opens with that exact marker, it skips the post, so a run that stopped after replying can simply run again.
  4. It sets the thread. It resolves or unresolves the thread, or leaves it alone for kept.
  5. It reads both back. It exits 1 when the reply does not open with the marker or the thread's resolution is not the one the result asks for.

True means resolve, False means unresolve, and None means leave the thread alone. The CLI takes its --result choices from these keys.
THREAD_QUERY returns the fields this function reads. I ran the query read-only against a real finding thread on this repository.
This is the retry path. The marker includes the result, head SHA, and model, so a reply on a later head or with another result is posted again.

groups.title: Permission rules
groups.kicker: The allow rule that project init adds for settle
intro: project init adds rules to your own Claude Code settings and Codex rules so that the review loop's GitHub writes are not refused by the host's automatic approval. settle posts a reply and resolves threads, so it joins publish, hold, finish, and summary publish in that list.
Anyone who ran init before this change now sees project review rules exit 1 until they run init again in a terminal.

files.note: Adds Bash(project review settle *) to RULES and a matching Codex prefix_rule, and updates the messages that list the commands.
Updates the expected rules, and builds the rule-missing cases from RULES so a new rule is covered without another hand-written case.

groups.title: Skill and documentation
groups.kicker: The review skill and CLI reference now point to settle
intro: The review-pr skill now tells the reviewer to write the reply to a file and run settle, and never to type the marker or call the resolve mutations through gh api. The method's withdraw step does the same, which also fixes an example marker there that lacked model=. docs/cli.md documents the command.
